newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU consumers urge child-targeted advertising curb.
newsitem.headline: EU consumers urge child-targeted advertising curb.

text.p: European consumer organisations on Monday urged the European Union to legislate against what they called increasingly diverse and devious methods of advertising aimed at children.

"Children are subjected to commercial pressure in almost every aspect of their daily lives: on television...at the sports club, playing games, eating breakfast, on their way to school, at school," Jim Murray, director of the consumer lobby BEUC, said.
"However, children do not have the same capacity to understand the commercial aim behind these marketing practices as adults do and therefore are more vulnerable," he added.

Murray, commenting in a statement on the results of a pan-European survey on children between the ages of six and 12 and advertising, said it was becoming increasingly difficult even for adults to identify advertising, let alone children.

The study showed that EU regulation had failed to keep up with increasingly sophisticated and often more covert marketing techniques, according to the BEUC, which groups national consumer organisations.

It said the techniques involved in-school marketing, children's clubs, contests, sponsorship of children's events, direct mail, teleshopping, offering free gifts, and promoting a product by linking it to a favourite children's movie or toy.
The group said that, even in cases where children could spot the advertising, they would be unable to develop a questioning attitude towards it until they were 11 or 12 years of age.
BEUC said it was seeking restrictions on in-school marketing and direct marketing in particular.
